metadata.description: This synthesis evaluates 7 pre-registered criteria for the load-smoothing hypothesis across 4 experiments covering 335 treebanks. Results: 0 criteria fully confirmed, 1 partial pass (novelty R²), 1 weak pass (α=1 control), 1 inconclusive (IC independence), and 4 failures (coverage, monotonicity, modality, case-marking). The primary empirical finding is a strong typological split (VSO>SVO>SOV) with a 1.58 SD gradient, which is explicitly exploratory and post-hoc. The head-initial-only IMB variant provides a mechanistic explanation for the SOV pattern via 68% peak IMB reduction. Of 8 reviewer critiques, 3 are fully resolved and 5 partially addressed. Major paper revisions needed: reframe as exploratory, drop failed predictions, add confirmatory/exploratory distinction.
metadata.what_paper_can_claim: The paper can claim: (1) A strong typological split exists in load-smoothing behavior: VSO languages show substantially higher real LLF than projective baselines (median d=1.039), SVO languages show near-zero difference (d=0.134), and SOV languages show reverse patterns (d=-0.546). (2) The head-initial-only IMB variant captures novel signal beyond DD statistics (R²=0.8827 < 0.90), particularly for head-initial dependencies. (3) This variant explains the SOV anti-smoothing pattern via 68% reduction in peak IMB. (4) IC and temporal overlap are partially independent (bidirectional test p=3.09e-07), though effects vary in direction across languages. (5) Head-final dependency proportion correlates strongly with the load-smoothing differential (r=0.501).
metadata.what_paper_cannot_claim: The paper cannot claim: (1) Universal load smoothing — only 31.4% of treebanks exceed d>0.2, far below the 70% threshold. (2) Monotonically increasing convexity effects — the residualized test fails. (3) Spoken modality shows greater smoothing — only 3/7 pairs support this. (4) Case-marking or DOM predict smoothing — both show null results. (5) The typological split is a confirmed pre-registered finding — it is explicitly exploratory and the VSO anchor rests on n=7 treebanks. (6) A clean negative control at α=1 — d=-0.0847 is small but not zero.
